author: Autodesk
description: This graph demostrates using RBD to scatter and settle instances.
documentation:
## Scatter and Settle (simulated)

### What it does
This graph uses the RBD system to scatter objects on to a terrain with physics. Once simulated the positions can be cached on the final frame and used in a environment.

### Inputs and outputs
This graph is self-contained, the terrain is generated in the ***generate_terrain*** compound, the rocks generated in the ***create_instance_geometry*** and those are fed into the RBD solver. The graph outputs MtoA compatible render geometry.

### How it works
A set of points are generated (***generate_points***) with geometry instanced on the points (***create_instance_geometry***). The instances have rigid body properties added to them (***set_rigid_properties***) and them simulated inside a static collider to keep all the instances inside the bounding volume. The rigid body settings are changed to enable faster settling. This graph settles in approximately 350 frames. The changed settings are *sleep_linear_threshold*, *sleep_linear_threshold*, *gravity* and *solver_iterations*.

metadata.description: This graph demostrates using RBD to scatter and settle instances.

_notes.text:
This is the bounding box of the ground element (terrain), scaled in the y-direction.  This is then set as a static collider.

This bounces any edge instances back into the range of the terrain, both optimizing simulation and providing more instances to settle.

Because the aim of this graph is to scatter and settle, the rigid body properties and solver settings are set for speed of completion, rather than a good looking simulation.

*sleep_linear_threshold* and *sleep_angular_threshold* have been increased to aid in quick settling.
*friction_scale* has also been increased.
*gravity* and *solver_iterations* have been increased to aid in quick and accurate settling.

These three custom fields allow more control over the displacement.  Feel free to dive into them and investigate.

By adding fields together a more complex displacement is created.

This compound generates the instance points for the rigid body system.

The *point_scale* and *point_orientation* properties are randomized here.

The length of the *point_scale* gives the *point_size* attribute, which is then remapped to provide the RBD mass scale.

Because the scatter should happen above the mesh, this section removes all faces below a height threshold.  This threshold is provided by the highest generated face, with a constant subtracted from it.  Any faces above the final threshold is filtered from the terrain mesh and used as a base for the *scatter_points*.

# how to make some rocks

In this loop, the incoming base mesh is used to generate a basic cell noise, then displaced by that noise.

The ***for_each*** loop is controlling how many objects are output to go into the instancer.

_backdrops.title: Assign material using generated color for render

_notes.text:
Cellular noise, also known as Worley noise or Voronoi noise, creates distinct cell-like patterns by randomly scattering points and calculating the distance to the nearest point.

This compound generates the scattered points.
The distance from every point to the closest random point generated earlier.
The raw distances are adjusted based on an input curve, remapped to a -1 to 1 range and output to become the cell-noise displacement.
